subject: Meteorology
title: Tropical Cyclone Forecasting
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tropical Cyclone Forecasting.

hook.text: Track forecasts have improved dramatically—but intensity forecasts still lag behind, frustrating forecasters.

buildup.text: The average 3-day track error has shrunk from 600 km in the 1970s to about 150 km today—a huge improvement.

discovery.text: Intensity prediction struggles because it depends on inner-core processes too small for most models to resolve.

twist.text: The forecast cone shows probable track—but people often ignore the width, focusing only on the center line.

climax.text: Ensemble and AI models are narrowing the intensity gap—but rapid intensification remains hard to predict accurately.

punchline.text: We know where it's going—but how strong? That's still tough.

quiz.question: Why is tropical cyclone intensity harder to predict than track?
options: Critical inner-core processes are too small for most models
